aspects.says: An invariant spanning two separately atomic variables can be seen broken by a reader between the two writes, so each part being atomic doesn't make the pair consistent.
basis: section:Each Step Other Threads Can Run Between Multiplies the Schedules: 6 for synchronized, 1,124 for Lock-Free
section:In the Simple Design the Race Has No Schedule, and Its Correctness Argument Is One Sentence

aspects.says: The simple design can be slower under heavy contention, and the decision weighs measured capacity against the stated load.
basis: section:Simplicity Costs Throughput Under Contention: Measure It Against the Load You Have

aspects.says: A thread waiting on a monitor or a java.util.concurrent lock is reported with the holder's name; a thread spinning on a hand-rolled atomic lock shows as RUNNABLE with no owner.
basis: section:A Thread Dump Names a Monitor's Holder; a Hand-Rolled Lock Shows Only Busy Threads

aspects.says: A synchronized method or block releases its monitor when the body throws; a hand-written lock is released only by a finally the caller wrote.
basis: section:A Thread Dump Names a Monitor's Holder; a Hand-Rolled Lock Shows Only Busy Threads

aspects.says: When every read and write of the shared fields holds one lock, or the state is one immutable value swapped atomically, a reader sees the state from before or after an update, never half of each.
basis: section:In the Simple Design the Race Has No Schedule, and Its Correctness Argument Is One Sentence

aspects.says: Every point where another thread can run between two steps of a shared operation multiplies the schedules: one step per method gives 3! orders for three calls, split steps give many more.
basis: section:Each Step Other Threads Can Run Between Multiplies the Schedules: 6 for synchronized, 1,124 for Lock-Free

aspects.says: A stress test runs the schedules timing makes likely, so it seldom meets a race that an exhaustive model finds in a large share of schedules.
basis: section:A Stress Test Samples the Likely Schedules, So It Seldom Hits the Broken Ones
